blocks.heading: Not a car.
paragraphs: Boat glass is often curved and set into a gasket at angles automotive film was never cut for. RVs bring their own mix of flat cab glass, small awning windows and sometimes a full wall of side glass.

On the water, glare comes up off the lake as well as down from the sky, and a closed cabin or a parked RV can bake all day with nobody there to crack a window. Ceramic film cuts glare and blocks UV on all of that glass.

blocks.heading: Is there a tint law for boats?
paragraphs: Nevada's window tint statute, NRS 484D.440, is written for motor vehicles on the road. It does not address watercraft, and we are not going to stretch a car and truck law to cover a boat. For an RV, ask us about legal shade options for your vehicle. See Nevada tint law for what the statute covers.

items.question: When is the best time to tint a boat?
items.answer: A lot of boat and RV film work happens before the season gets going, when a boat or a rig is being readied after it has sat for a while.
